alerts.title: Carbamazepine co-administration may reduce dolutegravir levels and cause virologic failure
alerts.message: Guidelines state that carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid instead of carbamazepine with DTG. Patient EX4 has been on TDF/3TC/DTG since 2022 with viral load suppressed (<50 copies/mL) on 2025-09-01, but carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily was started two weeks ago and viral load is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL. The temporal association with carbamazepine initiation is strong, and adherence is reported as good, so the reduced DTG exposure is a plausible cause. Non-drug causes of viral rebound should still be considered, and the guideline advises repeating viral load after enhanced adherence support.

evidence.recommended_action: Avoid carbamazepine with DTG; use valproic acid as the anti-epileptic if possible. Discuss with neurology urgently. Provide enhanced adherence support and repeat viral load in 2-3 months per guideline.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with neurological signs and hyponatraemia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic range 4-12) with nystagmus, wide-based gait, tremor, headache and dizziness, plus sodium 128 mmol/L. These findings are consistent with carbamazepine toxicity, which commonly causes ataxia, nystagmus and hyponatraemia, and the clinician plan is to reduce the dose and repeat the level. Sodium valproate is a co-medication and can also contribute to tremor and ataxia, and hyponatraemia has other causes that were not investigated in the notes.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce or hold carbamazepine per neurology and repeat level. Investigate hyponatraemia further and review valproate contribution to tremor and gait disturbance.

alerts.title: Monitoring gap: no documented repeat viral load or ALT follow-up plan
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend routine viral load monitoring every 6 to 12 months and a plan to repeat viral load after detectable results. The clinician plan addresses carbamazepine but does not include a repeat viral load, adherence support, or ALT follow-up. ALT is 68 U/L today, and the plan does not document review of this value.

evidence.recommended_action: Add repeat viral load in 2-3 months with enhanced adherence support, and review ALT and liver function during follow-up.
